title: Contributor Lifecycle Compass: Onboarding, Role Ladders, and Benefit Navigation
author: Asha Patel
summary: A single reference that maps a contributor's lifecycle at Redwood: from hiring and early onboarding through role ladders, promotion criteria, benefits enrollment windows, and practical use of internal tools. This compass unifies checklists, handoffs, and measurable expectations so hiring managers, people-ops partners, and new joiners can operate from the same playbook.
audience: New joiners, hiring managers, people-ops, hiring/recruiting, engineering managers, ICs planning role transitions
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates processes and living artifacts that guide contributors from offer acceptance through promotion or transition. It emphasizes measurable expectations, clear handoffs, and tool-enabled checkpoints. Use this compass as the canonical flow; team-specific deviations must reference and link back here.

Key principles:
- Single source of truth for lifecycle milestones (offer -> 1:1 cadence -> calibration -> promotion).
- Minimum friction: default tool flows and templates for access, training, and role ramp.
- Transparency: promotion criteria are objective and documented; managers record evidence in the calibration workspace.
- Safety net: defined reboarding and off-boarding steps ensure continuity.

1) Hiring & Offer -> First 2 Weeks (Rapid Enablement):
- Owner: hiring manager + people-ops onboarding partner.
- Objectives for new joiner: gain account access, join key meetings, deliver first merged change, and complete required compliance training.
- First-week checklist (actionable):
  1. Day 0: Equipment shipped, credentials email, and access RBAC request created (owner: IT).
  2. Day 1: Welcome standup with manager; review Role Brief and 90-day success milestones.
  3. Day 2–3: Core tool walkthrough (Git, infra CLI, CI dashboard, internal docs) with buddy.
  4. Day 4–5: Small end-to-end task assigned and merged.
  5. End of week 1: 30-minute alignment sync with people-ops to confirm benefits enrollment steps and payroll setup.

2) 30/60/90 Ramping Framework (sample expectations):
- 30 days: Understand codebase ownership boundaries, submit 1 non-trivial PR, and complete mandatory security/evals.
- 60 days: Independently own a small feature or operational runbook and shadow incident rotations as an observer.
- 90 days: Deliver a scoped project to production or launch an internal-facing tool; documented lessons learned; manager submits 90-day review.

3) Role Ladders & Promotion Criteria (common engineering ladder condensed):
- L1 - Associate Contributor: Contributes to team tasks, seeks feedback.
- L2 - Contributor: Delivers features with guidance, demonstrates solid engineering craft and code reviews.
- L3 - Senior Contributor: Owns medium-sized areas, mentors others, influences design decisions.
- L4 - Staff/Principal: Cross-team impact, technical strategy leadership, measurable product/infra improvements.

Promotion evidence checklist (minimum):
- Three cross-functional artifacts (design doc, postmortem, shipped project).
- At least 6 documented peer reviews with substantive feedback.
- Manager narrative aligned to rubric sections (craft, impact, leadership, scope).

Calibration process (high level):
1. Manager compiles evidence in the calibration workspace (link: /calibration-workspace).
2. People-ops schedules panel and distributes rubric 7 days prior.
3. Panel provides ratified level and feedback notes; people-ops records outcome and next steps.

4) Benefits & Perks Reference (enrollment windows and quick actions):
- Enrollment windows:
  - Health/Dental/Vision: Enrollment within 30 days of start date for full coverage; annual open enrollment each November.
  - 401(k): Auto-enroll opt-out within 7 days; match policy described on benefits portal.
  - Parental leave and family support: Submit notice to people-ops at least 60 days before planned leave when possible.

- Quick actions and links:
  - To enroll in health plan: benefits.redwood/internal/enroll (submit SSN and dependent docs).
  - Commuter and home office stipend: submit claim via expense portal within 90 days of purchase.

5) Internal Tools & Access (practical commands, templates, and ownership):
- Primary tools referenced here:
  - git (code hosting): repo naming convention: rwd-<team>-<service>.
  - infra-cli (internal): infra-cli auth login --team <team> ; infra-cli request-access --resource <resource> --reason "onboarding"
  - SSO portal: sso.redwood/corp -> request MFA device enrollment if not auto-provisioned.
  - Console dashboards: console.redwood/models and console.redwood/billing (manager-level view).

- Example RBAC access template (to paste into infra-cli ticket):
  "Request: repo access
   Team: <team>
   Repo: rwd-<team>-<service>
   Role requested: write
   Justification: <first week task>
   Expiration: 90d"

- Sample CLI snippet to set up local dev environment (bash):
  # Install and authenticate
  curl -fsSL https://internal.redwood/install-dev.sh | bash
  infra-cli auth login --sso
  make workspace-setup

6) Manager Handover & Role Transition Playbook:
- Trigger: manager change, role expansion, internal transfer.
- Steps (numbered):
  1. Outgoing manager fills Handover Form (template link: /handover-templates) within 3 business days.
  2. Schedule overlap meetings: 3 sessions (context, active projects, people).
  3. Update ownership in repo/team manifests and on-call schedules.
  4. People-ops verifies compensation/benefit continuity and updates payroll where applicable.

7) Onboarding SLOs and Escalation Paths:
- SLOs (targets):
  - 95% of new joiners have core tool access within 48 hours of start.
  - 90% complete mandatory compliance training within first 7 days.
  - 80% complete a merged PR within 14 calendar days.

- Escalation flow if SLO missed:
  1. Notify people-ops onboarding partner and hiring manager.
  2. If unresolved after 48 hours, escalate to Head of People-ops.
  3. Document incident and update onboarding runbook with root cause.

8) Reboarding and Returnship Guide (for long leaves):
- Purpose: reduce cognitive load on returners and minimize restart time.
- 4-week staged reboarding plan: admin reactivation (week 0), buddy pairing and sandbox tasks (week 1), project ramp and syncs (weeks 2–4).

9) Knowledge Capture & Handoffs (templates):
- Ship a 1-page role brief covering:
  - Primary responsibilities
  - Active projects and deadlines
  - Key stakeholders and communication channels
  - On-call rotation expectations and runbook links

10) Ownership, SLAs, and Contact Points:
- People-ops onboarding partner: Asha Patel (primary).
- Hiring escalation: Marco Ruiz (Head of Talent).
- Benefits and payroll questions: payroll@redwood.internal.

Appendix — Access Matrix (ASCII table):
| Resource                  | Default Owner         | Typical Access Granted | Time-bound by default | Request command example |
|-------------------------: | --------------------- | ---------------------: | --------------------: | ----------------------- |
| Code repos (team)         | Team lead             | write                 | 90d                  | infra-cli request-access --resource repo:rwd-team-service |
| Production infra (K8s)    | Platform SRE          | read                 | 30d                  | infra-cli request-access --resource cluster:<name> --role read |
| Billing console           | Finance lead          | view                 | 365d                 | request via console.redwood/billing |

Feedback or corrections: open a ticket in the People-ops board (board id: PEOPLE-2029) or email people-ops@redwood.internal.
